label: All data is synthetic and describes no real campus.
layout_note: All findings are from the current trunk-and-branch layout. Only the T = 8,760 attempt is from the earlier street-grid layout (commit 6fd4ac9).
host_load_note: The machine was shared and busy during the benchmark sweep: the 1-minute load average ranged from 17 to 102 (median 55) on 192 logical CPUs. All timings were taken on a loaded host.

findings.title: The GPU crossed over in the number of periods, not in network size
findings.text: At a matched tolerance of 1e-8, with every repeat solved on both devices and residuals matched, the GPU was faster at T = 24, 168 and 720 on the demo campus, so it crossed over at or below T = 24; horizons between 1 and 24 hours were not run. It was slower at all seven single-period network sizes, from 1.34 to 7.88 times the CPU time.

findings.title: At T = 720 every GPU repeat was faster than every CPU repeat
findings.text: At T = 720 the GPU median was 9.47 s against 426.0 s on the CPU, with all five repeats solved on both devices. At T = 24 (1.13 s against 5.82 s) and T = 168 (3.59 s against 52.8 s) the GPU median was lower, but two of five GPU repeats at each horizon were much slower than the rest.

findings.title: GPU iteration counts vary between identical runs
findings.text: At T = 720 the GPU took between 88 and 307 iterations on identical input, and every repeat solved. The CPU took the same number every time.

findings.title: Default GPU runs reached the requested tolerance
findings.text: With default settings every synchronous GPU repeat reached 1e-8. With asynchronous cuDSS one repeat at T = 168 stopped at the acceptable level.

findings.title: The GPU regularizes on most iterations
findings.text: With default settings the GPU applied inertia regularization on 88% of iterations on the demo campus, against 52% on the CPU. At T = 24 the figures were 94% and 67%. The cause was not isolated.

findings.title: T = 720 used about 36 GiB of GPU memory
findings.text: Peak GPU memory of one solve in a fresh process was 788 MiB on the demo campus, 2,852 MiB at T = 24, 11,926 MiB at T = 168 and 36,824 MiB at T = 720.

findings.title: Time to first solve is longer on the GPU
findings.text: A fresh process took 93.9 s on the GPU and 20.1 s on the CPU to finish its first two demo campus solves (medians of three runs).

not_run.status: Not run; the crossover in the number of periods is located only as at or below T = 24
Attempted once on the earlier layout (commit 6fd4ac9), neither device finished; not run on the current layout

not_run.item: Augmented KKT system on the GPU
Asynchronous cuDSS in the strict runs

roadmap.needs: Reliable GPU convergence at T = 8,760, steadier iteration counts than the 88 to 307 seen at T = 720, and a factorization that fits in GPU memory; T = 720 already used about 36 GiB.
Scenarios that share one sparsity pattern, and convergence of each scenario without manual restarts.
GPU convergence on the longer records the CPU solves, within GPU memory.
Models that ExaModels can evaluate on the GPU, and function evaluation becoming a large share of solve time.
